candidates.name: A2A Python SDK TaskStore / AgentExecutor

evidence.claim: The official executor separates execution/cancellation from event publication; TaskStore is a distinct server concern.

risks: Python server integration would add an execution/persistence boundary beside the Rust host.
Protocol records alone do not establish UAR mailbox crash recovery or external exactly-once effects.
candidates.decision_rationale: Reference lifecycle separation; adapt cand-001 persistence/thread host with durable correlation and acceptance intent. Do not install the Python SDK.

candidates.name: OpenTelemetry GenAI agent/tool conventions

evidence.claim: The attribute registry provides tool identity conventions; the former agent-span page now redirects readers to the dedicated GenAI repository.

risks: Telemetry is not the authoritative ordered task ledger.
Convention movement/stability must not change existing event wire fields.
candidates.decision_rationale: Keep existing RuntimeStep and tracing/OTLP dependencies. Add host correlation fields and optional convention mapping; no new exporter or observability service.

candidates.name: Anthropic skill-creator evaluation methodology

evidence.claim: The source separates trigger positives/near-miss negatives and outcome assertions, tracks timing/token comparisons, and separates training from held-out cases.
Skill-local license is Apache-2.0; repository root metadata alone reported no license.

risks: Its Claude-specific trigger execution is not UAR scope/permission behavior.
Tuning on certification cases would contaminate evaluation.
candidates.decision_rationale: Reference held-out trigger/outcome methodology; adapt current skill activation fixtures and exhaustive oracle. No upstream scripts are copied or executed.

candidates.name: Ragas faithfulness / claim decomposition

evidence.claim: Faithfulness decomposes an answer into claims and assesses support in supplied context; it is not an access-control mechanism.

risks: Model entailment is fallible and does not prove truth or tenant authorization.
Direct Python dependency would duplicate the governed inference boundary.
candidates.decision_rationale: Reference claim-level support; extend UAR verification with governed Liter extraction/entailment plus deterministic source/version/authorization checks. Model judgments remain labeled advisory; malformed/unknown evidence abstains.

candidates.name: Inspect AI external-agent evaluation

evidence.claim: Task construction accepts custom solver/agent and scorers; evaluation exposes repeated epochs and retained logs.

risks: Adopting a second runner adds Python packaging and risks exercising an adapter instead of the UAR host.
It cannot automatically supply UAR-specific deny, receipt or budget oracles.
candidates.decision_rationale: Reference solver/scorer/log separation; adapt existing Rust eval runner with a governed target and deterministic host fixtures. External Inspect integration is unnecessary for these exit criteria.
